headline: Tk 276 crore: ACC approves case against Hasina, Rehana
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission has approved a case over the alleged embezzlement of CSR funds meant for the Bangabandhu Memorial Trust.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has approved a case against ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, her sister Sheikh Rehana, and former Exim Bank chairman Mohammad Nazrul Islam Mazumder.
The case centers on the alleged embezzlement of Tk 276.30 crore in corporate social responsibility (CSR) funds.
These funds were collected from various banks specifically for the Bangabandhu Memorial Trust.
ACC Secretary Saidur Rahman Khan confirmed the development during a press briefing at the commission's headquarters.
The three individuals are named as the primary accused in the legal action regarding the misappropriation of these trust funds.

headline: Bill placed to abolish RAB and form Special Response Battalion
summary: The proposed SRB will replace the controversial elite force, transferring all its assets and manpower to a new specialized unit under the police force.
details: A bill was placed in the Jatiya Sangsad to abolish the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and establish the Special Response Battalion (SRB) as its replacement.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that a modern, professional, and accountable unit is necessary to ensure public security and effectively suppress organized crime.
The proposed law stipulates that all manpower, assets, funds, and records of RAB will be transferred to the new SRB.
The SRB will function as a specialized unit under the police force, with its own flag, emblem, and uniform, and will be empowered to investigate crimes, conduct searches, and arrests.
A multi-stakeholder grievance redress committee will be formed to handle public complaints and internal grievances of SRB members.

Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam and Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman supported the abolition of RAB, calling it a symbol of fascism, but demanded detailed parliamentary discussion before forming a new elite force.
The bill has been sent to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Home Affairs for scrutiny and a report within four working days.
Additionally, the Armed Police Battalion (APBn) Bill 2026 was also introduced to operate the APBn under the police force and grant it authority to investigate criminal offences.
caption:
RAB is being abolished. A new elite force, the Special Response Battalion (SRB), is proposed to replace it.

A bill was placed in the Jatiya Sangsad to abolish the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and establish the Special Response Battalion (SRB) as its replacement.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that a modern, professional, and accountable unit is necessary to ensure public security and effectively suppress organized crime.

The proposed law stipulates that all manpower, assets, funds, and records of RAB will be transferred to the new SRB.

The SRB will function as a specialized unit under the police force, with its own flag, emblem, and uniform, and will be empowered to investigate crimes, conduct searches, and arrests.

A multi-stakeholder grievance redress committee will be formed to handle public complaints and internal grievances of SRB members.

Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam and Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman supported the abolition of RAB, calling it a symbol of fascism, but demanded detailed parliamentary discussion before forming a new elite force.

The bill has been sent to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Home Affairs for scrutiny and a report within four working days.

Additionally, the Armed Police Battalion (APBn) Bill 2026 was also introduced to operate the APBn under the police force and grant it authority to investigate criminal offences.
